chapter_theme: Full Shakti (பூரண சக்தி): the goddess, Parashakti, is the Lord's own power and consort, mother of all within the bonds, the powers of knowledge, will and action, bindu and nada, and the light that rises through the lotuses of the yogic body. The chapter ends in praise of her names and a complaint that people speak of the Lord without knowing her.
structure_note: The verses are linked end to beginning (அந்தாதி: கும்பகம் closes 1126 and opens 1127, பாலன் closes 1134 and opens 1135, and so on). Roughly: Shakti and Siva in union and as the soul's parents (1125 to 1137); Shakti as bindu, nada and the light in the yogic lotuses (1138 to 1146); a run of praise verses naming her (1147 to 1153); and a closing reproach (1154).

1125.reading: Tirumular says he has measured the bounds of the wide world, its first Lord, and male and female in it, and that he measured them by examining and coming to know the Lord's grace.
1125.nuance: அளந்தேன் (I measured) opens all four lines. ஆணொடு பெண் may be the male and female of the world or Siva and Shakti; in a chapter on Shakti the second is likely, and the grace (அருள்) by which he measured is traditionally Shakti herself.

1126.reading: People have not known the Lord; the Shakti who brings about the ages joined him and that is fullness, and by the path the maiden who graces the companies of the meritorious brings, breath retention comes.
1126.nuance: பூரணம் (fullness) gives the chapter its title and is also the yogic term for drawing the breath in; with கும்பகம் (holding it) at the end, the verse seems to play on the stages of pranayama. கன்னி, the maiden, is a name of Shakti, ever virgin though consort. How the clauses connect is not clear from the verse.

1127.reading: The five elephants, their mahout with his goad, the jewel-crowned Lord and the lady who dwells sweetly in blissful union all merge and are lost in the union of love.
1127.nuance: கும்பக் களிறு ஐந்து, five elephants with swelling temples, are traditionally the five senses and the mahout the mind or the soul; கும்பம் picks up கும்பகம் from 1126. ஆயொழிந்தாரே, they became and ended, is read as absorption. The image is symbolic and the verse does not name its terms.

1128.reading: Our father can enter only into the love set in blissful union, and within the bond where people suffer in a mire of sorrow, Parashakti, my mother, is there in the very bones.
1128.nuance: The verse divides the parents: the father reached through love, the mother present inside bondage. என்பிற் is read here as 'in the bone', the body; it could also be a form of என்பது. The rhyme of அன்பு and என்பு is old in Tamil.

1129.reading: Once the conceit of saying 'my mother, my father' is gone, your mother and the Lord of the ages are both there; the great Nandi, joined with her as the abiding mother, stands as the mother after.
1129.nuance: The first line is clear: claiming the divine parents as one's own is a pride (செருக்கு) to be cut. The rest is obscure: பின்னம்மை may be 'the later mother' or பின்னம் (division) with அம்மை, and the subject of the last two lines may be Nandi or Shakti. The point the tradition draws is that the Lord is both father and mother.

1130.reading: The four-faced Brahma of the cool flower, the hundred on the earth and the teacher who dwells on the flower all come by the command of the lady who dwells on the tongue.
1130.nuance: நாமேல் உறைகின்ற நாயகி, the lady on the tongue, is the goddess of speech, here taken as Shakti. போதகம் may be 'teaching' or a 'teacher', and ஒரு நூறு (a hundred) is unexplained. The verse is nearly repeated as 1141.

1131.reading: Those who stay within, gathering the deluding mind into one and then knowing the Supreme, become that one themselves.
1131.nuance: Each line turns on a compound ending in -ஐயமாய் (ஆணையம், மாணையம், பாணையம், தாணையம்) whose senses are obscure; ஆணையம் picks up ஆணை from 1130. Only the outline (one-pointed mind, knowing the Supreme, becoming it) is fairly clear.

1132.reading: The mistress of the tattvas, arising of herself, lit the moon as the gods rose; with the light of a lamp that wells with honey, know the hall of the dance.
1132.nuance: மதியை விளக்கினள் can mean she lit the moon or she made the mind clear. மன்று is the hall where Siva dances, outward at Chidambaram or inward in the yogi's heart or head. மானே (O deer) addresses a woman, or names the goddess.

1133.reading: When the grace of the lady who is knowledge, within maya and within the five senses, comes to one, she stays filling the mind of those who know the knowledge that does not part, as their path.
1133.nuance: The verse makes Shakti knowledge both in maya and in the senses, so even bound knowing is hers. பிரியா அறிவு, knowledge that does not part, is traditionally knowledge inseparable from the Lord.

1134.reading: One who seeks out the long-haired lady dancing in the place where there is neither night nor day, and sleeps there with grace in silence, becomes a child that age does not touch.
1134.nuance: இரவும் பகலும் இலாத இடம் is traditionally the state beyond waking and sleep, or where the breaths called sun and moon cease. அரவம் is 'noise' but also 'serpent', so a reading in terms of kundalini is possible. பருவம் செய்யாத பாலன், a child that does not age, is the yogi's youth; பாலன் opens 1135.

1135.reading: He becomes a child, and with Parashakti, leaving bindu and nada behind, he stands as the Supreme itself, meeting the release that is the root.
1135.nuance: Bindu and nada are passed beyond, not reached, so they are here stages below release. தற்பரம் is the Supreme in itself. Whether the subject is the yogi of 1134 or the Lord is not settled by the verse.

1136.reading: Parashakti, standing with the Supreme, becomes the power of knowledge and the power of will, and when the power of action arrives she enters into all the rest.
1136.nuance: ஞானம், இச்சை and கிரியா are the three Shaktis of Saiva doctrine: knowing, willing and acting. The verse gives them an order, action last, through which she reaches everything else.

1137.reading: No one perceives that the lady, like fragrance in a flower, and he stand together in one form; when they mingled, like an embryo forming, our father stood with his thought set on her as on fortune.
1137.nuance: மருவொத்த can be 'like fragrance' (inseparable from the flower) or 'fitting'. கருவொத்து may be 'like an embryo' or 'in accord with the cause'. திரு may be Lakshmi, fortune or simply the sacred. The plain point, that Siva and Shakti are one form, is clear.

1138.reading: The Siva-Shakti who moves within thought spread out as bindu and nada; she is the moon-ground, the one with matted hair, the pure one, of the nature of both end and beginning.
1138.nuance: சந்திர பூமி, சடாதரி and சாத்தவி are names of the goddess; சாத்தவி may be 'the sattvic one' or a form of Shambhavi. சிந்தையின் உள்ளே places the cosmic bindu and nada in the mind.

1139.reading: No one knows the reversed way of the nectar-breasted lady who stays quiet; steady, with the light of a good lamp, she wells up for those who have the inner sight.
1139.nuance: அமுத பயோதரி, she whose breasts are nectar, is a name of the goddess. மாறி இருந்த வழி, the turned-back way, is traditionally the reversed course of breath or kundalini. உள்ளுடையார் may be those with inner vision or those who hold her within.

1140.reading: The Lord who owns all, the fire, the light of Rudra, rides the bull and shines; the base fall away, and the practitioners who see him become his dwelling place in their hearts.
1140.nuance: சாதகர் are practitioners of a discipline (sadhakas). The last two lines are compressed and the relation of கடையவர் போயிடும் to what follows is unclear.

1141.reading: Her dwelling above is the six-petalled lotus; above the earth the petals number in hundreds; the merit that dwells on the flower has come, the lady of fresh bangles who dwells above the earth.
1141.nuance: The petalled lotuses are traditionally the chakras of the yogic body; the counts (ஆறிதழ், பழினெட்டு, இருநூறு) can't be fixed from this text. The verse repeats the frame of 1130 almost line for line, with petals in place of Brahma.

1142.reading: Because the lady of fresh bangles stays where the Supreme is, as his firm banner and holy light, and comes shining as a creeper across the sky, the world moves on as the woman's creeper.
1142.nuance: கொடி means banner, creeper and, of a woman, slenderness; the verse plays on all three. The claim is that the world runs by her, as the creeper grows from its root in the Lord.

1143.reading: The flower moved as four and five, the maidens sat as eight and one, it spread its own way inside the lotus and followed the inner way, close to the light.
1143.nuance: Both pairs make nine; the maidens are commonly taken as the nine Shaktis seated in the heart lotus, eight round one. What the subject of படர்ந்தது and தொடர்ந்தது is (the flower, the light, the breath) is left open.

1144.reading: The stacked lotuses are the seat of the Primal one: one rises within the house of the body, one goes up to the crown of the head, and one presses upward in the triple square.
1144.nuance: முச்சதுரம் (triple square) is traditionally the base centre, drawn as a square; மத்தகம் is the head. The four kinds of lotus (அடுக்கும், எடுக்கும், மடுக்கும், முடுக்கும்) are a sound pattern whose technical sense is uncertain.

1145.reading: The sprouting flame that rose in the triple square ran until it had a place in every square, and passing the square of the hand to gain the inner light, she stayed in all of them.
1145.nuance: முளைச்சுடர், the sprout-flame, rising from the base square is traditionally kundalini. கைச்சதுரம் (square of the hand) is obscure. சதுரம் closes every line, picking up முச்சதுரம் from 1144.

1146.reading: She stayed with faces six and four; the breaths spread to every quarter, drew together to look at the pearl-bright face, and the nectar flowed down.
1146.nuance: ஆறொடு நாலாய் may be ten faces, one to each quarter, or six and four. தேறல் (honey, nectar) flowing அதோமுகம் (face downward) is traditionally the nectar from the crown. The final அம்பே may be 'arrow', 'water' or 'mother'.

1147.reading: Manonmani, with eyes like arrows and a waist slender as a twig, garlanded, her body like worked red gold and fragrant, speaks every day with her eyes on the Lord.
1147.nuance: மனோன்மணி is a name of Shakti in Saiva tantra, the power beyond mind. நவிலுகின்றாள் is 'speaks' or 'recites'; what she says is not given. The praise of her beauty follows the conventions of love poetry.

1148.reading: The great goddess of whom the four Vedas speak, clothed in garments, her feet covering the ground, stands in majesty over the world and the whole cosmos, adorned with the three lights.
1148.nuance: முச்சோதி, the three lights, are traditionally sun, moon and fire. நான்மறைச் சத்தி may mean the Shakti of whom the Vedas speak or the Shakti who is the Vedas. The second line's sense is unclear.

1149.reading: I say praise to her who can adorn our Lord of the worlds, who can shape the countless cosmic eggs within, and who can adorn the light of the mandala.
1149.nuance: புனைதல் (to adorn, compose) and வனைதல் (to shape, as a potter shapes clay) carry the verse: she is both the Lord's ornament and the maker of worlds.

1150.reading: I hail the mother, mistress of the worlds, the young girl of rare penance who stands within my strength, the jewelled one of fair brow who put away anger, the one of fresh bangles who drives Death away.
1150.nuance: அருந்தவப் பெண்பிள்ளை recalls the goddess as a girl doing penance to win Siva. என் ஆற்றலுள் நிற்கும, standing within my strength, makes her the poet's own power. சீற்றங் கடிந்த can mean she has put away anger or that she quells it.

1151.reading: The bangled beauty from whom joy rises, the lady Tripura of fair form, Ganga, destroys the deeds of her devotees, thick as brushwood, and is also the Primal one.
1151.nuance: சுகோதய சுந்தரி and திரிபுரை are names of the goddess. செடியார் வினை may be deeds thick as a bush or sinful deeds (செடி, sin). The third line (சேர்வரை என்றென்) is obscure.

1152.reading: She of soft sound, a tender creeper of the sky, she of many sounds, a fruitful creeper, drove out the doll of mean sound and entered the mind as the doll of mighty sound.
1152.nuance: இசை is sound and also fame, and பாவை a doll or a woman. The four kinds of sound may be the levels of speech from subtle to gross, as tradition reads such lists; புல்லிசை may equally be ill repute driven out of the mind. புகுந்தானே has a masculine ending where புகுந்தாளே would be expected.

1153.reading: Our Lord is himself the goal of penance; when he conceives and makes the world, Parashakti joins him and runs through it above and below, and that very one becomes the life of all.
1153.nuance: பாவித்து, conceiving or contemplating, makes creation an act of the Lord's thought, with Shakti as its extension. ஆவிக்கும் may be 'for the soul' or 'that gives life'. The opening word தாவித is obscure.

1154.reading: Not knowing him, people call him this or that; they do not see the cause that stands for release to come, and they neither consider the constancy of the great lady with flowered tresses nor examine and know.
1154.nuance: The chapter closes with a reproach: speaking of the Lord without knowing his Shakti is to miss the cause through which release (கதி) comes. திதம் is steadiness or standing.

links.note: The two verses share a frame (தார்மேல்/தாமேல் உறைவிடம், பார்மேல், பூமேல் உறைகின்ற ... வந்தனள்): 1130 fills it with Brahma and the goddess of speech, 1141 with the lotus petals and the bangled lady. They may be variants of one verse.
Both make the goddess and bindu one: 1925 sets Mahamaya, the goddess of speech and kundalini within bindu, 1138 has Shakti spread out as bindu and nada.

Both cut a pride (செருக்கு) voiced as possession: the Kural's 'I' and 'mine', Tirumular's 'my mother, my father' said of the divine parents. Tirumular extends the Kural's renunciation of ownership to the soul's claim on God.

Both set love (அன்பு) against bone (என்பு). For the Kural a body without love is bone wrapped in skin; Tirumular has the father reached through love and the mother present in the bone within bondage. The pairing depends on reading என்பிற் as 'in the bone'.

Both join penance, power and the defeat of death: the Kural says those who gain the power (ஆற்றல்) of austerity can leap past death; Tirumular's goddess of rare penance stands in his power (ஆற்றல்) and drives Death (கூற்றம்) away.

source_issues: 1129: line 3 reads உரைசெய்Yயும் with a stray Latin Y; read உரைசெய்யும்.
1147: line 4 reads றா\ளே with a stray backslash; read றாளே.
1149: line 3 மண் லடத்தொளி is probably மண்டலத்து ஒளி, split wrongly.
1144: line 3 மத்தகச் தேசெல is malformed, perhaps மத்தகத்தே செல.
1146: line 2 (பரந்தன வாயு திசை தோறும்) is short by a foot; a word may be lost.
1141: பழினெட்டு is not a standard form (perhaps பதினெட்டு); 1130 and 1141 look like variants of one verse.
1131 and 1153: the -ஐயமாய் compounds of 1131 and the opening தாவித of 1153 are obscure and may be corrupt.
